I would keep to the cropping pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to use the full year, and at my age I would rather choose steady grain crops with familiar field work than try something risky or labor-heavy. I would use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, put most of my fertilizer into the wheat-maize rotation, irrigate wheat more because spring here is often dry, and keep maize management simple with no-tillage after wheat harvest so I can save time and labor. I would aim for stable yield, not the highest possible yield, because I care more about getting the crop in and out on time and avoiding major losses from drought, weeds, insects, and disease.
